messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER - severity: high
oncall-bot: service: model-serving-tp-3 (tensor/pipeline cluster) - increased 5xx and stuck requests, auto-escalation: oncall

oncall-bot: https://internal.incidents/1890123456 - please ack and post mitigation steps :rotating_light:

alex: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs from the affected pods.

maya: seeing repeated NCCL timeouts + communicator aborts in pod ml-serve-22. also intermittent CUDA OOM on gpu0. past 10 mins: 3x "NCCL WARN" then 2x "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" and a container restart.

alex: paste the relevant log snippet?

maya: here, from pod ml-serve-22/container-runtime.log:
```
[2026-03-15T12:04:34Z] NCCL WARN Call to deviceCommInit failed: NCCL_COMM_ABORTED
[2026-03-15T12:04:34Z] NCCL INFO rank 2 failed to connect to rank 0
[2026-03-15T12:04:35Z] cudaDriverGetVersion = 12070
[2026-03-15T12:04:35Z] CUDA ERROR 2: (out of memory)
[2026-03-15T12:04:36Z] killing process 2145 due to OOM
[2026-03-15T12:04:40Z] container restarted by kubelet
```

maya: also noticed a spike in interconnect errors on node gpu-node-17 (nvlink errors in dmesg).

ryan: thanks. I'm seeing the same stack across 3 pods in that placement group - likely a multi-gpu rendezvous failure rather than a single model OOM. Could be noisy neighbor leading to backlog + KV cache blowout causing memory spike.

alex: immediate mitigation options:
- drain gpu-node-17 and evacuate pods to other nodes (prefer avoid mass restarts)
- scale down TP partition size to force fallback to smaller tensor shards (if runtime supports)
- reduce per-request batch size / concurrency at gateway to lower instantaneous memory pressure
- restart affected containers after node drain

alex: I'm going to cordon + drain node to remove the noisy host. will do graceful eviction with 30s grace to let in-flight requests attempt retry.

ops-bot: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

oncall-bot: update: escalation -> sre-lead notified.

sre-lead: joining. Quick question: do we have recent kernel/NVIDIA driver rollouts on gpu-node-17? need to rule out driver regression.

maya: no driver rollout in last 48h. last infra change was a kubelet bump 3 days ago but it's targeted. nvlink counters show errors though.

ryan: during drain, I'm reducing gateway concurrency for model-serving-tp-3 to 4 (was 12) to reduce influx of new TP requests.

alex: pods are re-scheduling to gpu-node-22 and gpu-node-10, one pod failed to join the NCCL communicator after restart. log shows: `rendezvous failed: NCCL_UNREACHABLE` then `fallback to single-gpu` triggered by runtime fallback policy.

customer-eng: we've seen increased 503s for 12 paying customers using the large-TP pipeline. they reported latency spikes and failed completions. I've DM'd affected accounts and put them on status page with mitigations.

sre-lead: good. capture impact: number of requests failed ~ 1.2k over 20m, max p95 latency 3.2s -> clients saw 503s. mark as partial degradation.

alex: after moving pods, memory pressure reduced. however one node (gpu-node-10) shows a recurring CUDA OOM within the worker loop when attempting allreduce across 4 ranks. replicating snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:14:51Z] allreduce start (ranks 0-3)
[2026-03-15T12:14:53Z] NCCL INFO  -> timeout waiting for operation queue
[2026-03-15T12:14:53Z] CUDA ERROR 700: an illegal memory access was encountered
[2026-03-15T12:14:53Z] process 2198 killed
```

ryan: illegal memory access tends to be a kernel/driver or HW issue. nvlink ECC counters show 9 corrected errors on gpu-node-10 in last hour.

alex: decision: roll pods to single-GPU model variant for the affected shard group to restore serving while we diagnose multi-GPU fabric. Initiating runtime fallback to single-gpu variants for shards [tp-10..tp-13]. this will increase latency but avoid allreduce hang.

ops-bot: applying runtime config: `redwoodctl rollout set model-serving-tp-3 --variant single-gpu --shards tp-10,tp-11,tp-12,tp-13`

oncall-bot: action: customer impact mitigation - single-gpu fallback in progress. estimated switch time 4m.

maya: single-gpu fallback applied, pods now stable. error rate dropping.

sre-lead: starting post-handoff checklist:
- collect full core dumps and allreduce traces from affected containers (alex)
- schedule hardware health check for gpu-node-10 and gpu-node-17 (ops team)
- add NCCL communicator aborted alert and track NVLink ECC counters (infra)
- revisit gateway concurrency defaults and add autoreduce when NCCL errors spike (runtime)
- customer followup and incident RCA (customer-eng + product)

alex: grabbing cores now, attaching storage to preserve. also uploading NCCL debug traces to /s3/incidents/1890123456/nccl-traces.tar.gz

ryan: putting a 1-hour maintenance window and marking cluster as degraded in console. will monitor for reoccurrence.

customer-eng: notified customers that mitigations applied and that we might be throttling concurrency for stability. asked them to reach out for any data loss — none reported.

sre-lead: handing off to night oncall. next oncall: ryan (starts 2026-03-15T18:00Z).

ryan: acked. summary for handoff: multi-gpu NCCL communicator failures + CUDA OOMs tied to NVLink ECC increases on two nodes. Mitigation: drained gpu-node-17, rolled shards to single-gpu variants, reduced gateway concurrency. Customer impact: partial degradation, ~1.2k failed requests, 12 customers affected. Follow-ups created: #INC-1890123456 RCA, hardware check ticket HW-5421.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated, monitoring.

alex: thanks everyone. will attach logs + mitigation timeline to the RCA ticket. suggest we add canary for NVLink ECC trends.

sre-lead: agreed. planning an on-call hotfix runbook for NCCL communicator aborts (quick steps: reduce gateway concurrency, apply single-gpu fallback, cordon node, hardware check).

ryan: will watch overnight. ping me if errors reappear. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: thread closed by oncall-bot (status: monitoring).
